answer: One practical defense is a time-locked bond: every new agent must escrow tokens that stay frozen for ninety days before it can vote on attestations. Each fake identity needs its own bond, so a thousand sock puppets freeze a thousand deposits, and the lockup pushes any payoff past the attacker's horizon. Splitting one budget instead yields a dune of identities, wide but shallow, each too thin to sway a vote. Honest agents gain weight slowly, like water carving karst.
